_comment: THE INVENTORY LEDGER (#915 Wave 4). One of five ledgers under tests/; every count here is DOWN-ONLY and every named exception carries an issue and an expiry. Two shapes live here and the difference is deliberate. An EXCEPTION section (skips, envRed, advisory) names individual sites: each one needs `issue` and a deadline — `expires` (a date) or, for env-red, a `revisitTrigger` naming the event that retires it. A POPULATION section (sleeps, hygiene, commentDensity) budgets a whole measured count rather than a list of exemptions: there is no per-site row to attribute, so the SECTION carries `issue` and `expires`, the date by which the ratchet itself is re-argued. `naCells` is a reference to tests/claims.json#naCells, which carries its own 183-day re-verification ritual. Each scanner still owns its own detection and its own --write, and each writes only its own section; lint:ledgers owns the shared shape, the direction, and the deadlines. See TESTING.md 'The ledgers'.

skips._comment: The skip budget (#656 Layer 2). Every deliberate hole in the suite — test.skip / describe.skipIf / .todo / runtime t.skip() / a CENTRAID_* or CLAWGNITION_* opt-in env gate — is inventoried here with an OPEN tracking issue and a reason. scripts/test-report/skip-inventory.mjs discovers the population by scanning; validate-matrix.mjs (in check:pr) fails on an uninventoried skip, on a stale entry, and whenever the count differs from _budget. _budget is DOWN-ONLY: deleting a skip must lower it in the same change, and adding one costs an explicit hand edit plus an issue. Keys are <path>#<ordinal> (nth skip site in that file) so they survive line drift; `line` is informational and refreshed by `node scripts/test-report/skip-inventory.mjs --write`. A skip site also forbids its file from backing a computed-solid matrix cell — see scripts/test-report/matrix-grades.mjs.
skips.approvedDeviation: #1120 removes the 22 `sites` whose files no longer exist (the retired apps/** and packages/** test trees, plus the tests/perf, tests/scale and scripts/gateway-package files deleted with them) and lowers `_budget` 25 to 3 with them, exactly the count of rows removed; no surviving row exists to move. Prior: #799 — the budget falls 30 → 25 (down-only). The five retired sites were all permanent skips against the served-app plane: the three desktop copilot cases (7.2–7.4) drove a panel inside the app iframe, builder publish drove the app builder, and the app-bundle case gated on the shipped Photos + kit dirs the whole-graph asset bundler read. Stages 2 and 3 of #799 delete those surfaces, so the holes close by removal rather than by fix.

envRed._comment: Deterministically-environment-red inventory (#781). A test whose law cannot hold in a known environment — the wal-shipper [G4] class, fixed as an instance in #782 — is neither a flake (tests/quarantine.json) nor merely a declared skip (tests/skips.json): quarantine would exclude it everywhere to silence one environment, and the skip budget records the hole without the environment shape or a revisit discipline. The mechanism is therefore a REQUIRED env guard (skipIf / runtime t.skip — which also lands in the skip budget) plus this ledger: every environment-predicate guard site (process.platform / process.arch / process.getuid comparisons in test files, discovered by scripts/test-report/env-red-inventory.mjs over the same globs as skip-inventory) must be recorded here with the guarded test, the human-readable predicate, the guard mechanism, an OPEN tracking issue, and an expiresAt date or a revisitTrigger sentence. An expired entry is a hard failure; _budget is DOWN-ONLY — the way to shrink this file is the #782 move: rewrite the test so the environment stops mattering. Keys are <path>#<ordinal>; `line` is informational and refreshed by `node scripts/test-report/env-red-inventory.mjs --write`.
envRed.approvedDeviation: #1120 removes the 4 `sites` whose files no longer exist (packages/server and packages/vault integration tests of the retired TypeScript gateway) and lowers `_budget` 6 to 2 with them, exactly the count of rows removed.

sleeps._comment: The fixed-sleep ratchet (#781). A fixed sleep bets that the awaited work finishes inside a literal; the bet is invisible until it loses on a slower runner. Every site is counted per file by scripts/test-report/sleep-inventory.mjs and the total is DOWN-ONLY — measured above `_budget` fails, and measured BELOW it also fails, so removing a sleep forces the ceiling down in the same change. A population budget, not a list of exemptions: the rows are counts, not attributed waivers, so the deadline below is the section's.
sleeps.approvedDeviation: #1120 removes the 25 `sites` whose files no longer exist (the retired apps/** and packages/** trees and the tests/agent-e2e-pairing flow deleted with them) and lowers `_budget` 36 to 0 with them, exactly the 36 fixed sleeps those rows counted.

hygiene._comment: The hygiene ratchet (#781). Two TESTING.md conventions that lint cannot own — 'prefer specific matchers over toBeTruthy()' and 'assert outcomes, not mock calls' — measured as counts over **/*.test.{ts,tsx} by scripts/test-report/hygiene-ratchet.mjs and enforced DOWN-ONLY: a measured count above its budget is a hard failure (the convention cannot regress quietly), and a measured count BELOW its budget is also a failure, because the budget must always equal the measured count — improving the suite forces you to tighten the ceiling in the same change. `node scripts/test-report/hygiene-ratchet.mjs --write` does that reconciliation and can only ever LOWER a number; raising one is a deliberate, reviewed edit. Lint cannot enforce either rule: oxlint's prefer-to-be-truthy / prefer-to-be-falsy are off (#573) because their autofix runs the WRONG direction, rewriting the house-style toBe(true) into the strictly weaker toBeTruthy(); and prefer-called-with rewrites toHaveBeenCalled() into toHaveBeenCalledWith(), which asserts the mock was called with zero arguments. toBeTruthyFalsy counts .toBeTruthy( and .toBeFalsy(. toHaveBeenCalled counts the whole toHaveBeenCalled* family EXCEPT bare .not.toHaveBeenCalled(), which is exempt on purpose: there is no toHaveBeenCalledWith equivalent of 'never called', so naming arguments there would weaken the assertion rather than sharpen it (QUALITY.md #496: of 1,023 sites, all 186 bare ones were negated and zero positive bare calls remain). Seeded 2026-08-14 from the counts measured on that tree; the chip-away is #496's hygiene workstream, and every entry here is expected to fall. Raised 840->845 in the same #781 wave that seeded it: the Places mobile-seat tests (#781, places views) assert navigation through five toHaveBeenCalledOnce/toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith sites on the stubbed navigator, where the call with its exact route and params IS the observable outcome; a reviewed raise, not --write.

commentDensity._comment: The comment-density ratchet (#861). Doctrine governs what a comment may say; this budget governs how much. The metric is CHARACTER SHARE — non-whitespace characters inside TypeScript-parser comment ranges over non-whitespace characters of the whole file — measured by scripts/check-comment-density-ratchet.mjs over every git-tracked packages/** and apps/** .ts/.tsx file except .d.ts. Characters, not lines: a line count is gamed by fusing three comment lines into one wrapped sentence, and holding whitespace out of both sides keeps blank lines and reflowing out of the number. Every measured file carries a pin [commentChars, totalChars] and enforcement is DOWN-ONLY: any rise in a pinned file's share fails the gate, compared by integer cross-multiplication so a re-pin is exact and no regression rounds into the noise. Downward re-pins are free — `node scripts/check-comment-density-ratchet.mjs --write` recomputes every pin, adds new files, prunes deleted ones, and refuses to raise a pin, so --write cannot launder a regression. A deliberate raise is a hand edit to this file carrying an approved-deviation note in the issue receipt. A file with no pin and at least 40 non-blank lines fails above a 15% share; the global target is <=10% and the gate prints the running figure on every run, pass or fail. `allowlist` exempts a named file from the 15% cap ONLY, never from its pin, for registries where the prose IS the payload — it is the pressure valve that exists so nobody deletes load-bearing rationale to hit a number.
commentDensity.approvedDeviation:
#1120 removes the 3861 pins and 74 allowlist rows of `files` and `allowlist` whose paths no longer exist: every apps/** file and every packages/** file outside packages/design and packages/test-kit, left behind by the retired web, desktop, extension and TypeScript-package shells (#1020 and earlier). The 93 surviving pins and 5 surviving allowlist rows are untouched: removals only, no pin moves and none rises. Prior: #1099 removes the pins of the 162 files Tally left behind when it left v0 (PR #1112): every packages/blueprints/apps/tally, apps/mobile/src/apps/tally and packages/vault tally file, its tests, and the tally-named files beside them. Removals only: the files no longer exist, no surviving pin moves, and the allowlist loses its one Tally row. Prior: Seeded 2026-08-25 on the #861 Wave 0 tree: 3,638 files, global character share 24.31%, global line density 14.83%, 1,975 files above the 15% cap. Every pin here is expected to fall — the sweep waves under #861 are what lower them, and --write re-pins them as they do. Raised 2026-09-01 for #903 (PR 911): 92 pins hand-raised, all of them files that commit rewrote. Two thirds of the rise is a DENOMINATOR effect rather than new prose — #903 deleted code (a shelf, a band tab, four copy strings shortened under the U4 ratchet, share logic consolidated onto one seat) while its rationale comments stayed, and the share is a ratio. The rest is doctrine the receipt argues is load-bearing: ruling G-revoke on the audience-side hard delete, the absent-is-not-empty rule the Shared shelf turns on, and the folders-scheme join that made a delivered copy invisible. Cutting these back to the old pins meant removing about 33,000 comment characters across 99 files; the receipt records that trade being refused, and 2,467 characters WERE cut from the files this PR authored before the raise. Every raised pin is down-only again from here.
 Raised again 2026-09-01, same PR, for three more files — every one of them a DENOMINATOR move rather than new prose. `packages/vault/src/index.ts` and `packages/vault/src/grant/grant-store.test.ts` rose because `ensureFulfillment` was DELETED from them (it had no production caller after #903 replaced it with `setFulfillmentState`), so removing code raised the share of the comments left standing: index.ts moves 11.02% to 11.02%, a rise only integer cross-multiplication can see. `packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts` is the schema/export audit OWNER — a register whose comment share is 42% by design, and whose whole contract is that every fingerprint move gets a recorded ruling. The #903 ruling is that there is nothing to carry, and writing it down is the one thing the schema/export ratchet demands of this PR. Raised again 2026-09-01 for #903 (PR 911): 2 pins, both load-bearing invariants found by running the seat against a live seeded gateway. apps/mobile/src/lib/phone-link.ts 12.84->13.87% names why the gateway's hostname must precede the vault's name when recording `desktopName` — taking `vaultName` first drew two indistinguishable "Personal / Personal" switcher rows. apps/mobile/src/navigation.ts 34.98->35.34% is a types file whose whole rise is ONE JSDoc line saying why the Settings screen is `SettingsHome`. Both were trimmed hard first — phone-link peaked at 16.90% and came down to 13.87%, under the 15% cap — and neither file is allowlisted.

allowlist.packages/design/src/density.ts: spacing rung registry; the rulings are the payload (#861)
allowlist.packages/design/src/palette.ts: palette registry; per-value derivations are the payload (#861)

fileSize._comment: The file-length inventory. `max-lines` in oxlint.config.ts caps a source file at 625 lines (#615's limit, previously enforced by the retired governance-kit `repo-hygiene` directive). scripts/lint-oversized-files.mjs reads `sites` and oxlint turns the rule off for exactly those paths, so every file predating the rule is exempt by name rather than by an inline suppression. `_budget` is the row count and is DOWN-ONLY: splitting a file removes its row and lowers the budget in the same change, and exempting a new file costs a hand edit plus an `approvedDeviation`. The number on each row is the file's length when it was inventoried — informational, not a per-file ceiling. A new file gets no row and no door.
fileSize.approvedDeviation: #1120 removes the 119 rows of `sites` whose files no longer exist (the retired apps/** and packages/** trees, and the tests/ and scripts/ files deleted with them) and lowers `_budget` 128 to 9 with them, exactly the count of rows removed. The 9 surviving rows are untouched and none rises. Prior: #1099 removes the three Tally rows of `sites` (packages/blueprints/apps/tally/queries/dashboard.ts, packages/vault/src/commands/tally.ts, packages/vault/src/commands/tally-organize.ts) as Tally leaves v0 (PR #1112), and lowers `_budget` 131 to 128 with them. The files are deleted; no surviving row moves.

naCells._comment: REFERENCE, NOT A COPY (#915 Wave 4). The deliberate n/a cells live at tests/claims.json#naCells, where #915 Wave 3 absorbed them from tests/na-cells.json. They are governed by a RE-VERIFICATION ritual rather than by a budget — a row unreviewed for two quarters fails `bun run check:na-cells` (scripts/audit-na-cells.mjs, 183 days) — and the count is deliberately NOT down-only: an honest impossibility is not debt. Named here so this file is a complete index of the repo's inventories.

advisory._comment: #892 Phase 3 — every CI step that ANNOUNCES it will never fail carries an owner, an issue and a date by which somebody decides whether it should stay advisory. scripts/ci/advisory-expiry.mjs fails on a missing entry, a missing field, a past `revisitBy`, or an entry naming a step that no longer exists. This is the same discipline the quarantine ledger, tests/env-red.json and every tighten-only budget already apply; a non-blocking annotation had none, and it is the place a real regression hides longest precisely because its normal state is 'there is output'.
